conf.description: Trellix ePO, device-control, syslog-cef: CEF header + fixed-order extension-key regex_extract (same envelope grammar as ens-threat; no Cribl CEF-parse function exists), severity invert, ThreatHandled bool, DOMAIN\user split; tags collection_transport for downstream dedup against the richer jdbc-sql feed per recommendations.direct.cribl.

conf.comment: trellix-epo/device-control/syslog-cef. Same CEF envelope as ens-threat (the Automatic Response reuses the registered-server/threat-event property set), so the extension key order below is assumed identical to that sibling pipeline's verified order; unused envelope keys (AnalyzerDetectionMethod, AnalyzerDATVersion, SourceIPV4, TargetHash) are consumed positionally but not captured, since this dataset's map doesn't name them. ThreatActionTaken is a resource key (IDS_ALERT_ACT_TAK_*) but the map gives no device-control-specific literal codes for the block/read-only reactions that matter here, so it is passed through raw rather than guessed (README gap). TargetFileName is legitimately empty for plug-and-play/device-load blocks - that is not a parse failure. Tags collection_transport=syslog-cef per recommendations.direct.cribl so this row can be recognized as a duplicate of the richer jdbc-sql record and lose on conflict.

functions.description: identify technology, dataset, format, and parsing approach

conf.regex: /^CEF:\d+\|[^|]*\|[^|]*\|[^|]*\|[^|]*\|[^|]*\|[^|]*\|DetectedUTC=(?<DetectedUTC>.*?) ReceivedUTC=(?<ReceivedUTC>.*?) ThreatEventID=(?<ThreatEventID>.*?) ThreatName=(?<ThreatName>.*?) ThreatType=(?<ThreatType>.*?) ThreatCategory=(?<ThreatCategory>.*?) ThreatSeverity=(?<ThreatSeverity>.*?) ThreatActionTaken=(?<ThreatActionTaken>.*?) ThreatHandled=(?<ThreatHandled>.*?) AnalyzerName=(?<AnalyzerName>.*?) AnalyzerDetectionMethod=.*? AnalyzerDATVersion=.*? SourceIPV4=.*? SourceProcessName=(?<SourceProcessName>.*?) SourceUserName=(?<SourceUserName>.*?) TargetHostName=(?<TargetHostName>.*?) TargetIPV4=(?<TargetIPV4>.*?) TargetUserName=(?<TargetUserName>.*?) TargetFileName=(?<TargetFileName>.*?) TargetHash=\S*$/

functions.description: split the CEF pipe-delimited header (discarded) from the ePO threat-event extension key=value pairs; only the keys this dataset's field table names are captured as named groups, the rest of the fixed envelope is matched but not extracted

decode the partial/unmapped extension fields (severity invert, ThreatHandled bool, DOMAIN\user split) reading the ORIGINAL vendor names before rename, set _time from DetectedUTC (not syslog receipt time) per the field table, and tag event.dataset and collection_transport
batch-rename status:mapped extension fields that need no further transform to their ECS target
Re-nest flat dotted keys (data-maps canonical step)
